artifact.self_contained_problem:
A II_1 factor is a von Neumann algebra M with trivial center, equipped with a faithful normal tracial state τ, that is infinite-dimensional and not of type I. It is called amenable if it is hyperfinite (equivalently, isomorphic to the unique hyperfinite II_1 factor R).

A II_1 factor N has the Haagerup property if there exists a net (φ_i) of normal completely positive τ-preserving maps N → N such that each φ_i is compact (i.e., extends to a compact operator on L^2(N,τ)) and φ_i → id_N pointwise in ‖·‖_2.

A II_1 factor M has property (T) if every M-M bimodule H that almost has a central tracial vector (in the sense that there exists a net of unit vectors ξ_i ∈ H with ‖xξ_i − ξ_i x‖ → 0 for every x ∈ M) actually contains a nonzero central tracial vector.

Given a unital inclusion N ⊆ M of tracial von Neumann algebras, we say that N is existentially included in M if for every existential formula φ(x_1,…,x_n) in the language of tracial von Neumann algebras and every tuple a_1,…,a_n ∈ N one has
   φ^N(a_1,…,a_n) = φ^M(a_1,…,a_n),
i.e., the inclusion preserves the values of all existential formulas with parameters in N.

Question: Suppose N is a nonamenable II_1 factor with the Haagerup property, and N is existentially included in a II_1 factor M. Can M have property (T)?
